items.evidence: Refuted rejection ground: the rival splitting 36:2-4 from 36:5-7 is dismissed because no addressee change, date frame or fresh word-event formula falls between them. The bytes contest the first term. 36:2 opens the divine speech to Jeremiah with קַח לְךָ֮ מְגִלַּת סֵפֶר֒ (oshb:Jer.36.2, byte), a second-person singular imperative with the ethical dative; the span's own splice at 36:5 is וַיְצַוֶּ֣ה יִרְמְיָ֔הוּ אֶת בָּר֖וּךְ לֵאמֹ֑ר (oshb:Jer.36.5, byte) - a new speaker (Jeremiah) and a new addressee (Baruch). An explicit addressee or scene shift is a tier-1 internal cut class, so the rival is refused on precisely the ground the bytes hand it. The boundary may still stand on the frame-plus-speech default that keeps a commission with its narrative frame, but that is not the warrant given, and a replacement warrant has to pass the test that killed the original. Shape count: the device prose keeps the date frame apart from what it calls the book's two named word-event formulas. The byte-derived inventory carries THREE never-blended shapes - vayehi debar-YHWH (sweep: 21 verses), ha-davar asher hayah el-Yirmeyahu (sweep: 11 verses), asher hayah debar-YHWH el-Yirmeyahu (sweep: 4 verses). The omitted third shape is the one nearest in wording to this verse's own clause, הָיָ֞ה הַדָּבָ֤ר הַזֶּה֙ אֶֽל יִרְמְיָ֔הוּ מֵאֵ֥ת יְהוָ֖ה לֵאמֹֽר (oshb:Jer.36.1, byte), so dropping it weakens the very disambiguation the sentence performs. Ordinal not carried: the literature-type calls this the first public reading, but the reading inside the span is the infinitive construct לִקְרֹ֥א בַסֵּ֛פֶר (oshb:Jer.36.8, byte) under the finite וַיַּ֗עַשׂ בָּרוּךְ֙ בֶּן נֵ֣רִיָּ֔ה (oshb:Jer.36.8, byte) - a dateless compliance summary - while the narrated reading verb וַיִּקְרָ֨א בָר֥וּךְ בַּסֵּ֛פֶר (oshb:Jer.36.10, byte) falls outside the span; that declared false positive is refuted. Gloss extent: the two overlapping splices at oshb:Jer.36.1 each carry an English extent reaching a word the splice itself does not hold. items.evidence: Second reading: the rival is discussed as separating the relay from what the prose calls Baruch's own second reading. The bytes carry the reading of the scroll as a finite verb exactly once here: לִקְרֹ֥א בַסֵּ֛פֶר (oshb:Jer.36.8, byte) is an infinitive construct complementing the finite וַיַּ֗עַשׂ בָּרוּךְ֙ בֶּן נֵ֣רִיָּ֔ה (oshb:Jer.36.8, byte) in a compliance summary that carries no date, and the reading at oshb:Jer.36.13 is likewise an infinitive construct, while the one finite reading verb of the scene is וַיִּקְרָ֨א בָר֥וּךְ בַּסֵּ֛פֶר (oshb:Jer.36.10, byte) (sweep: 1 finite reading verb in MT 36:8-36:13). Whether the summary anticipates the dated reading or reports a separate event is a held reading; it is asserted here as settled, with no disclosure. Interval: the span is described as a full year on from the preceding dated notice. The fourth-year notice at oshb:Jer.36.1 carries a year with no month; the notice at oshb:Jer.36.9 carries a year and a ninth month. The bytes leave the interval undetermined, so the stated span of time is not sourceable from them. Verified sound: the front seam at oshb:Jer.36.9 is a verse-initial date frame, so classified in the byte-derived date inventory; the rear seam at oshb:Jer.36.14 carries a real addressee turn in the bytes - the relay is to the princes at 36:13, the sending is to Baruch at 36:14; the span mark-absence statement is true (sweep: 0 PE, 0 SAMEKH, 0 paseq segs, 0 kq notes in MT 36:9-36:13), and the upstream setumah at MT 36:8 is correctly typed; all four splices reach byte tier; the reduced confidence and the flagged frontier are consistent with the thinness of the interior evidence. items.claim: The rival is rejected on a ground the span's own full-verse splice contradicts - these two verses are dense with personal names - and the name-form disclosure carries a recurrence claim with no sweep digit and an undercount of the attested spellings.
items.evidence: Refuted rejection ground: the larger-unit rival is refused because these verses report the reign and its character with no named individual or dated moment. The dateless half is true - this verse is not among the 19 classified date candidates and carries no year token - but the named-individual half is refuted by the very splice quoted in full at byte tier: the opening verse names five persons, among them תַּ֗חַת כָּנְיָ֨הוּ֙ בֶּן יְה֣וֹיָקִ֔ים (oshb:Jer.37.1, byte) and נְבוּכַדְרֶאצַּ֥ר מֶֽלֶךְ בָּבֶ֖ל (oshb:Jer.37.1, byte), and the prophet is named in the second verse (oshb:Jer.37.2). The refuted half is the one doing the work against verse 3, whose own opening is asserted without any quoted bytes while confidence is held high. Date wording: the rationale says the reign is dated to a king installed by Babylon; there is no date token in the verse, and the relative clause identifies the installer, not a date. Digit-less recurrence: the device prose says the resh-family Nebuchadnezzar spelling recurs through the chapters ahead, with no sweep digit and no unit named, in a record that does supply a digit for the predecessor's name form; that spelling stands in 29 verses (sweep: 29 verses). The same sentence calls the alternative a nun-family spelling, singular, where the byte inventory carries two nun-family spellings - the fuller form (sweep: 6 verses) and the vav-less defective form at 28:11 and 28:14 (sweep: 2 verses) - beside a plene byform of the resh family at 49:28 that rides on a doubled ketiv/qere note; a four-spelling hazard is reported as two. Verified sound: the predecessor digit is right token-bound (3 verses: 22:24, 22:28, 37:1); a bare consonantal substring sweep returns 4 because the Jeconiah form at 24:1 contains that string, and the figure given survives that trap. The three name forms named for this one king match the inventory. The transition is correctly read as a regnal notice and not as a word-event onset - the bytes carry a wayyiqtol accession clause, no word-event formula. Marks: the upstream setumah at MT 36:32 is correctly typed, and the in-span absence statement is true (sweep: 0 PE, 0 SAMEKH, 0 paseq segs, 0 kq notes in MT 37:1-37:2). The parent frame is correctly carried across the part seam rather than broken at it.
